title: Engine Emission Control: PCV Valve Location
introduction:
The large POWERED BY FORD lettering and round oil-filler cap make useful landmarks in this drawing. I start at the cap, then look above and to its left in this view for the blue-highlighted valve at the hose connection. Follow the callout line and match it with the description table to identify the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve.

The valve regulates crankcase-vapor flow into the intake system. Combustion gases that slip past the piston rings—blow-by—need a controlled route out of the crankcase to limit pressure and contamination buildup. The valve acts like a gatekeeper for that traffic; the connected hose carries the vapors along their route.

This is a component-location reference. Finding the valve does not establish its condition, and the drawing provides no access or removal sequence. For service work, use the [engine-specific PCV valve procedure](#/document/G1691483).

edits.why: This configuration label identifies the engine covered by the drawing. Ti-VCT means twin independent variable camshaft timing, which allows intake and exhaust camshaft timing to be controlled separately.
